stem: Meera notices that she looks like her parents, but her younger brother Aarav has a slightly different eye colour. Which statement correctly explains how reproduction produces both similarity and variation in a family?

options.text: Reproduction passes instructions from parents to children, and small changes in these instructions can cause variation.
Reproduction makes exact copies of the parents, so any variation must come from a completely separate process.
Reproduction only creates variation and plays no role in keeping children similar to their parents.
Variation appears only when the environment changes, and reproduction has nothing to do with it.

teacher.key_rationale: Inherited instructions from parents produce resemblance (continuity), while small changes in those instructions produce variation; only option A states both parts correctly. B denies that reproduction can create variation, C denies continuity, and D detaches variation from reproduction entirely.
